intro: Aggregate accuracy can conceal unequal errors across groups. A disaggregated audit reports selection, true-positive, and false-positive rates with their denominators.
task: Disaggregate selection and error rates by group, retaining denominators to expose groups with no eligible positive or negative examples.
requirements: labels and predictions are equal-length binary integer-valued vectors; groups is a same-length token list or tuple with at most 10000 nonempty strings. All may be empty.
Return a dictionary keyed by group with count, positives, negatives, selection_rate, tpr, and fpr. Compute rates independently within each group.
Define tpr as 0 when a group has no positive labels and fpr as 0 when it has no negative labels; returned denominators make these undefined-in-principle cases visible.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Keep label denominators separate
hints.body: TPR divides by actual positives; FPR divides by actual negatives.

hints.title: Return counts with rates
hints.body: A zero rate with no eligible examples should be distinguishable from zero observed errors.

explanation: Group rates expose differences that an aggregate metric can hide. Equal selection rates do not imply equal true-positive or false-positive rates, as the worked example shows.
These descriptive metrics do not establish a system as fair. The grouping, label quality, uncertainty, and consequences of decisions all affect how the audit should be interpreted.
